title: Section 83 — Marriage ceremony fraudulently gone through without lawful marriage

content.overview: BNS s. 83 — Marriage ceremony fraudulently gone through without lawful marriage.
content.study:
Introduction and meaning
Marriage ceremony fraudulently gone through without lawful marriage. BNS restatement of IPC 496. Elements are substantially the same; cite the BNS number for offences on or after 1 July 2024. BNS restatement of IPC 496. Cite the BNS number for facts on or after 1 July 2024.
In student language: BNS s. 83 is the rule on “Marriage ceremony fraudulently gone through without lawful marriage”. The section provides that whoever, dishonestly or with a fraudulent intention, goes through the ceremony of being married, knowing that he is not thereby lawfully married, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine. Do not stop at the heading. An examiner awards marks for the ingredients, the explanations and the illustrations, not for writing the title alone.

Why this is asked
Criminal law arguments turn on statutory ingredients. BNS s. 83 exists so that “Marriage ceremony fraudulently gone through without lawful marriage” has a closed legal test in Chapter V — Of Offences Against Woman and Child. An authoritative analysis defines the concept, lists every ingredient, walks the statutory illustrations, states exceptions, and applies the test methodically to facts.
Chapter setting: Sexual offences, assault, marriage, miscarriage, and offences against the child — placed first among the offence chapters.

learningObjectives: Master the elements of fraudulently or dishonestly undergoing a marriage ceremony knowing there is no lawful marriage.
Differentiate mock or sham marriage ceremonies from bigamy and deceitful cohabitation.
Analyze the mental state of dishonesty and fraudulent intent.
enhancement.definition: BNS s. 83 provides that whoever dishonestly or with a fraudulent intention goes through the ceremony of being married, knowing that he is not thereby lawfully married, shall be punished with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to seven years, and shall also be liable to fine.
enhancement.legalPrinciple: Criminalizes sham and mock marriage ceremonies where an individual abuses matrimonial rites with fraudulent intent knowing that no valid legal bond is created.
statutoryFramework: Chapter V — Of Offences against Women and Children, BNS s. 83 (corresponding to IPC s. 496).
Actus reus: Going through the ceremony of being married with knowledge of lack of lawful marriage.
Mens rea: Dishonestly or with fraudulent intention.
Punishment: Imprisonment of either description extending up to seven years, and fine.
essentialIngredients: The accused went through the ceremony of being married.
The accused knew that he or she was not thereby lawfully married.
The accused acted dishonestly or with a fraudulent intention.
enhancement.detailedExplanation: Section 83 targets sham or mock marriages. Unlike bigamy where the ceremony would create a valid marriage but for the subsistence of an earlier marriage, Section 83 applies where the ceremony itself is a hollow pretence that does not create a lawful marriage, and the accused knows this fact. The accused must act either 'dishonestly' (to obtain wrongful gain or cause wrongful loss) or 'with fraudulent intention' (to deceive and cause injury or advantage). For instance, an accused may stage a fake wedding to deceive the victim's family, gain access to property, or obtain social recognition, while secretly knowing that key legal or ritual requirements were omitted.
examples: Teaching example (Mock ceremony for property transfer): A man stages an elaborate ceremony with a woman before a bogus registrar knowing the registration is invalid, with the fraudulent intent of securing an inheritance contingent on marriage. He is liable under s. 83.
Teaching example (Dramatic performance vs fraud): Actors participating in a staged marriage for a theatrical film production do not act dishonestly or fraudulently; hence s. 83 does not apply.
distinctions: Section 83 vs Section 81: Section 81 requires subsequent cohabitation or sexual intercourse induced by deceit; Section 83 is completed the moment the ceremony is gone through with fraudulent intent.
Section 83 vs Section 82: In Section 82, the parties intend to marry and perform full rites, but the marriage is void due to a living spouse; in Section 83, the ceremony itself is a fraudulent sham.
problemApplication: Issue: Whether an accused who performed a mock wedding in a private club with fake officiants to convince the woman's parents to release dowry funds is guilty under s. 83.
Rule: Going through a mock marriage ceremony with fraudulent intent to secure financial benefits constitutes an offence under BNS s. 83.
Application: The accused knew the ceremony had zero legal validity and acted dishonestly to obtain money.
Conclusion: The offence under s. 83 is established.
